stage1_plan.missing_check: Ownership check for an existing comment: comment.UserID must match user.UserID unless the current user is a privileged moderator/admin in the same domain.
stage1_plan.insertion_location: views/comments.go, inside the `if commentIDStr != ""` block immediately after the `if comment == nil || comment.TopicID != topic.TopicID { ... }` validation and before `var quote string`.
stage1_plan.reused_project_semantics: Reuses the app's real context user (`user, _ := r.Context().Value(CtxUserKey).(*models.User)`), `comment.UserID` as owner, `user.IsSuperMod`/`user.IsSuperAdmin` as privileged-role bypass, `domain.DomainID` for same-domain moderation, and the project denial style `http.Error(w, http.StatusText(http.StatusForbidden), http.StatusForbidden)`. The guard shape mirrors the horizontal ownership/role check in `views/users.go` profileHandler.
stage1_plan.reason: The edit/delete flow only verifies that the URL comment belongs to the URL topic; it never verifies that the current user owns that comment. Thus any authenticated user can POST Update/Delete for another user's comment. Adding the ownership check after loading/validating the comment blocks horizontal modification before quote rendering and before the Update/Delete operations, while keeping authorized owners and privileged moderators/admins working.

stage2_patch.explanation: Added an ownership check in the editComment handler to prevent horizontal privilege escalation. The check verifies that the current user owns the comment being edited/deleted, unless the user is a privileged moderator or admin in the same domain. This guard is placed after comment validation and before any state-changing operations (Update/Delete) or rendering. It uses the existing denial style and role variables from the project.
